newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank leaves repo rate at 4.10 percent.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank leaves repo rate at 4.10 percent.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday set its weekly reverse repurchase operation at an unchanged, fixed 4.10 percent despite wide market expectations of a cut in the key interest rate.
The reverse repurchase operation will run from January 22 to January 29.
The Riksbank said primary dealers were invited to leave bids by 0900 GMT on January 21 at the latest.
The repo rate is the Riksbank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity.

A Reuters poll of 13 analysts found that 10 of them expected the Riksbank to lower the repo rate, most of them expecting the cut on Tuesday and most forecasting a cut of between 15 and 25 basis points.
But one of the analysts said the cut may not come until the Riksbank's board meeting on Thursday as the operation was too close to the announcement of December's consumer price index.
Figures released at 0815 GMT, 15 minutes before the repo announcement, showed the CPI fell by 0.2 percent in December for a year-on-year change of minus 0.2 percent.
This was the third consecutive month that Sweden has noted a negative annualised inflation trend.
The Riksbank board, which announces any changes to the interest rate corridor, will meet at 0745 GMT on Thursday.
The repo rate stands at the centre of the Riksbank's interest rate corridor that is marked out by the deposit and lending rates that stand at 3.75 percent and 5.25 percent respectively.
